# Fixed completed-run C1 callbacks

`completed_c1.run_fixed_c1_callbacks(stage, inventory, stage_directory, source_root, staging, *, deadline)` is a bounded, non-authorizing follow-on to [`completed_run.resolve_completed_run`](completed-run-README.md) and [`completed_validation.inspect_completed_run`](completed-validation-README.md). It accepts only the already-resolved completed-run record and its parsed 37-artifact inventory. The returned `C1CallbackProjection` records the fixed C1 callback output, source/run/attempt identity, the original aggregate archive and body hashes, and the recomputed body hash. It contains no admission, qualification, Trusted, coverage-credit, or gate-eligibility field.

The function reads the fixed fourteen `issue779-checkpoint1-selector-{selector}-{run_id}-{attempt}.zip` archives in source-owned selector order, compares their archive and member projections to the completed inventory, then extracts each into a new private invocation directory. It verifies that all fourteen `source.json` files are byte-identical to the resolved capture. It checks that each retained `result.json` has the expected selector, each build receipt records exactly the passed canonical `source_root`, and each `execution.json` has `workflow_identity` exactly `github-actions-{run_id}-{run_attempt}`. Relocation is rejected: the C1 retained validators use the recorded source-root path for source-bound lookups, so the validator must run with the exact original workspace path. The checkout itself is verified against the capture by the validator checkout's fixed current `binding.verify_source` before the captured source binding or C1 runner is executed.

The protected verifier must run from its independently trusted source checkout, while `source_root` names the exact original completed-run workspace. The function loads the captured `.github/issue779-checkpoint1/run-native.py` from that verified completed-run checkout and calls its fixed `aggregate` function synchronously. This executes the original per-selector `verify_retained_evidence` implementations and the original aggregate reconciliation. The C1 callback function accepts no caller-selected callback, module, selector list, or expected return rows. The aggregate archive body is independently checked for the captured head and capture digest, all fourteen selectors, the fixed sixteen-case set, `passed: 16`, `skipped: 0`, `exit: 0`, and false native-acceptance/coverage-credit flags. The projection keeps the original archive hash distinct from the archive body hash and recomputed body hash.

## Bounds and cleanup

The caller must supply one finite monotonic deadline that already accounts for the existing 120-second C1 reconciliation allowance and a five-second readback reserve. The C1 runner keeps its original deadline and joins synchronously. The validator adds only staging constraints: 64 MiB maximum for an extracted member, 512 MiB total expanded bytes across the fourteen selector archives, no more than the existing per-archive 8,192 ZIP members after counting implicit directories, and a maximum staging depth of 64 path components. These constraints prevent small ZIPs from creating an excessive implicit directory tree; they do not alter C1 execution, admission, coverage, or workload limits.

All invocation-created nodes are recorded by file descriptor identity as they are created. Cleanup uses directory-relative no-follow operations, removes only nodes whose identities still match, refuses substituted parents or files, and never recursively deletes unknown nodes. Cleanup runs to completion over the fixed maximum node inventory even if the callback deadline has elapsed, to avoid abandoning owned work. If cleanup cannot verify or remove every invocation node, the operation fails; if a callback already failed, that original exception remains primary and receives only a fixed cleanup-failure marker. The wrapper checks the original deadline again after cleanup before returning success.

The internal `_reconcile_callbacks(...)` helper exists for a mechanism-level replay harness that already has the fourteen extracted `native` receipt directories from original artifacts. It performs the same independent checkout, run/attempt, selector-order, source-root, workflow-identity, callback, and aggregate checks but does not own those input directories. The caller owns their lifecycle. Its result is likewise non-authorizing.

## What this slice proves

A successful call proves only that the source-owned original C1 retained-evidence callback aggregate ran against those fourteen fixed original selector receipts and matched the archived aggregate body. It does not validate the fourteen measured-chain archives, their paired EOF callbacks, C2 receipt/EOF checks, C3 application or lifecycle callbacks, either C4 account callback, Native.Tests data validators, the coverage/Codecov gates, or protected downstream acceptance. Those remain separate required checks in the [`57-group plan`](../../docs/plans/issue-779-evidencehost-test-plan.md) and must be orchestrated by a later fixed completed-run validator. This return value must never be passed to runtime admission or used to populate the accepted-proof registry.

The focused tests cover archive projection/extraction boundaries, implicit-node depth, source-root/workflow/selector identity rejection, cleanup on success and failure, inode substitution refusal, original callback exception preservation, module-state restoration, and the strict aggregate non-claim fields. Two synthetic 37-archive fixtures run the actual inventory inspection, projection checks, private file reads, ZIP extraction and cleanup, replacing only the final callback boundary. Other synthetic wrapper fixtures isolate lifecycle failures and substitutions. These fixtures do not establish a positive original callback result. A genuine positive callback result must come from the fixed replay helper against exact original retained artifacts on a Linux environment with the same recorded source-root path.
